sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，展示着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The situation here, it's a bad situation.
sentences.zh: 这里的情况，情况很糟糕。

sentences.en: I was born here.
sentences.zh: 我出生在这里。

sentences.en: I never saw a situation like this.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过这样的情况。

sentences.en: More than two weeks after one of the most consequential elections in Israel's history, there is still so much uncertainty among voters about who will lead the country.
sentences.zh: 在以色列历史上最重要的一次选举过去两周多后，选民们对于谁将领导这个国家仍感到非常迷茫。

sentences.en: 20 years.
sentences.zh: 20年了。

sentences.en: I think you have to go home.
sentences.zh: 我想你得回家了。

sentences.en: It seems like the longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, could be on the way out.
sentences.zh: 看起来执政时间最长的总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡可能要下台了。

sentences.en: I don't really know if I'm in favor or not of Eisenkot because it's very difficult for me to believe in anyone nowadays in Israel.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道自己是否支持艾森科特，因为如今在以色列，我很难相信任何人。

sentences.en: And so the spotlight has fallen on opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot,
sentences.zh: 因此，聚光灯落在了反对派领导人加迪·艾森科特身上，

sentences.en: who is trying to make all kinds of deals with disparate political parties who have different wants and different needs in order to actually build a coalition that could run the government.
sentences.zh: 他正试图与各怀心思、诉求迥异的政党达成各种协议，以组建一个能够执政的联合政府。

sentences.en: What I would like is the Israeli society to get unified and get together once and for all.
sentences.zh: 我希望以色列社会能一劳永逸地团结起来。

sentences.en: But the choices about who to partner with and how, they are just not simple.
sentences.zh: 但关于与谁合作以及如何合作的选择，绝非易事。

sentences.en: No, he has to compromise.
sentences.zh: 不，他必须妥协。

sentences.en: He has to go either with the religious or with the Arabs.
sentences.zh: 他要么必须与宗教派合作，要么与阿拉伯派合作。

sentences.en: And so today on the show, Jerusalem Bureau Chief David Hauptfinger explains the kinds of compromises that Eisenkot will need to make if he wants to run the country.
sentences.zh: 所以今天在节目中，耶路撒冷分社社长戴维·豪普芬格将解释艾森科特如果想治理国家，需要做出什么样的妥协。

sentences.en: It's Israel's last chance to become a country with some sort of sanity.
sentences.zh: 这是以色列成为一个理智国家的最后机会。

sentences.en: It's an insane place at the moment.
sentences.zh: 现在这里简直是个疯人院。

sentences.en: And what will happen if he can't pull it off?
sentences.zh: 如果他做不到会发生什么？

sentences.en: It's Friday, November 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月13日，星期五。

sentences.en: David Hauptfinger, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 戴维·豪普芬格，欢迎回到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: The last time we spoke, you had prepared us for an election that a lot of Israelis thought of as existential and one whose results were going to be kind of messy and unclear.
sentences.zh: 我们上次交谈时，你为我们预告了一场许多以色列人认为关乎存亡的选举，其结果可能会非常混乱且不明朗。

sentences.en: That seems to have borne out.
sentences.zh: 现在看来确实如此。

sentences.en: We're talking to you more than two weeks after the election.
sentences.zh: 我们在选举结束两周多后与你交谈。

sentences.en: We don't have a clear answer.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有明确的答案。

sentences.en: And the path forward, from what I can tell, is going to be not just complicated, but also, as you prepared us for,
sentences.zh: 据我所知，未来的道路不仅会很复杂，而且正如你所预言的那样，

sentences.en: have seismic political implications for a country that has been so long dominated by one guy.
sentences.zh: 对于一个长期由一个人统治的国家来说，这将产生深远的政治影响。

sentences.en: So catch us up, David, on what has happened since Election Day.
sentences.zh: 那么戴维，给我们讲讲选举日之后发生了什么吧。

sentences.en: So the election was huge.
sentences.zh: 这次选举规模巨大。

sentences.en: There was an incredible turnout in this election, but there was no clear winner.
sentences.zh: 投票率高得惊人，但没有明确的赢家。

sentences.en: Gotti Eisenkot, the leader of the opposition, was given the chance to form the government because he heads the largest coalition.
sentences.zh: 反对派领导人加迪·艾森科特获得了组阁机会，因为他领导着最大的联盟。

sentences.en: But who will be in that government?
sentences.zh: 但谁会进入那个政府呢？

sentences.en: It remains unclear and very much in doubt.
sentences.zh: 这仍然不清楚，而且充满了变数。

sentences.en: He would have to put together a coalition that is incredibly diverse and, in some cases, at odds with itself.
sentences.zh: 他必须组建一个极其多元化，甚至在某些方面相互抵触的联合政府。

sentences.en: That's an incredibly difficult thing to do, but he can't afford to fail.
sentences.zh: 这极其困难，但他输不起。

sentences.en: So he's got a month, a maximum of six weeks, to try to put together a government that can lead this country.
sentences.zh: 所以他有一个月，最多六周的时间，来尝试组建一个能领导这个国家的政府。

sentences.en: What happens if, at the end of that six weeks, he is unable to get a government together?
sentences.zh: 如果六周结束时他无法组建政府，会发生什么？

sentences.en: So if Eisenkot fails, it's likely that Netanyahu would be given the next chance to form a government.
sentences.zh: 如果艾森科特失败，内塔尼亚胡很可能会获得下一次组阁机会。

sentences.en: But four weeks, and then it could go to the parliament itself.
sentences.zh: 但只有四周时间，之后可能会交给议会本身。

sentences.en: The Knesset would have three weeks to choose a candidate.
sentences.zh: 以色列议会将有三周时间来选择候选人。

sentences.en: But if all of that fails, the parliament would dissolve, and we'd have three months until new elections are held.
sentences.zh: 但如果所有这些都失败了，议会就会解散，我们将迎来三个月后的新一轮选举。

sentences.en: Netanyahu is the caretaker prime minister.
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡是看守总理。

sentences.en: He's the incumbent.
sentences.zh: 他是现任者。

sentences.en: And if he remains the incumbent while we go to new elections, that gives him an enormous advantage and a much stronger shot at winning again.
sentences.zh: 如果他在我们进行新选举时仍保持现任身份，这会给他带来巨大的优势，并大大增加他再次获胜的机会。

sentences.en: — So what does Eisenkot actually have to do over these next four, or as you said, six weeks, to build a coalition?
sentences.zh: 那么艾森科特在接下来的四周，或者如你所说的六周内，到底需要做什么来组建联盟？

sentences.en: — So with the four parties that are squarely in his coalition right now, he has a total of 48 seats in parliament.
sentences.zh: 目前他的联盟中有四个核心政党，在议会中总共拥有48个席位。

sentences.en: Ideally, he comes up with a coalition that has 61 seats out of the 120 in parliament behind it, at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，他组建的联盟至少要拥有议会120个席位中的61个。

sentences.en: That's a simple majority, a real majority, in parliament.
sentences.zh: 那是简单多数，在议会中真正的多数。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's what he would love.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是他梦寐以求的。

sentences.en: But in this case, it seems really difficult to imagine how he could do that, because the parties that are available to him are really at odds in important ways.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，很难想象他如何做到这一点，因为他能争取的政党在重要问题上确实存在分歧。

sentences.en: They're ideologically diverse.
sentences.zh: 他们在意识形态上各不相同。

sentences.en: They're ethnically diverse.
sentences.zh: 他们在种族背景上也各不相同。

sentences.en: You talk about Congress as herding cats.
sentences.zh: 人们常说管理国会就像牧猫一样。

sentences.en: Imagine herding lions or tigers.
sentences.zh: 想象一下牧狮子或老虎吧。

sentences.en: — That's what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们所讨论的。

sentences.en: These are people who are, in some ways, fundamentally at each other's throats.
sentences.zh: 这些人，在某些方面，简直是势不两立。

sentences.en: — Okay, basically what you're describing is a really serious uphill battle to get people to come together to support him.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你描述的基本上是一场极其艰难的战斗，要让人们团结起来支持他。

sentences.en: — Yeah, and he has to both negotiate with all of them and then figure out a coalition that he wants to govern with from among them
sentences.zh: 是的，他既要与他们所有人谈判，又要从他们中间理出一个他愿意共同执政的联盟，

sentences.en: and work out the most favorable deal possible to allow him to achieve the goals of him and his core coalition partners.
sentences.zh: 并达成尽可能有利的协议，以实现他和他的核心联盟伙伴的目标。

sentences.en: So that's not an easy task to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是一件容易的事。

sentences.en: And, you know, it might seem like a month or six weeks is plenty of time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，一个月或六周的时间看起来很充裕。

sentences.en: But, you know, I think you could easily blow through all of that time and come up with nothing.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得他很容易就会耗尽所有时间却一无所获。

sentences.en: — Okay, so then, David, tell us about some of the different options that he actually has.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么戴维，告诉我们他实际上有哪些不同的选择。

sentences.en: Like, who could he potentially partner with?
sentences.zh: 比如，他可能与谁合作？

sentences.en: — So, first, we have to remember that in his campaign, Eisenkot made a lot of—well, he made several really serious promises to the voters.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们必须记住，在竞选期间，艾森科特向选民做出了许多——好吧，他做出了几个非常严肃的承诺。

sentences.en: And every one of those is going to make his life complicated.
sentences.zh: 而每一个承诺都会让他的处境变得复杂。

sentences.en: His options—you know, one of his options is something he ruled out in the campaign.
sentences.zh: 他的选择——你知道，其中一个选择是他在竞选中已经排除了的。

sentences.en: Working with Netanyahu himself, he could form a unity government.
sentences.zh: 与内塔尼亚胡本人合作，他可以组建一个联合政府。

sentences.en: You know, so he could go in with Netanyahu after having campaigned against him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他可以在竞选反对内塔尼亚胡之后，又与他联手。

sentences.en: For obvious reasons, that seems like a non-starter.
sentences.zh: 出于显而易见的原因，这似乎行不通。

sentences.en: — Yeah, I mean, it's frankly impossible to imagine now, not only because he campaigned against it, but because, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，坦率地说，现在很难想象，不仅因为他曾竞选反对过，而且因为，你知道，

sentences.en: I think it would be just seen as the ultimate betrayal of the voters.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会被视为对选民的终极背叛。

sentences.en: I mean, the entire opposition coalition, probably the top priority is getting Netanyahu and this government out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个反对派联盟的首要任务可能就是让内塔尼亚胡和现政府下台。

sentences.en: So bringing him back in or giving him a new lease on life would be just unforgivable.
sentences.zh: 所以让他回来或者给他第二次机会，简直是不可原谅的。

sentences.en: Moreover, it's hard to imagine Netanyahu agreeing to terms that Eisenkot could accept.
sentences.zh: 此外，很难想象内塔尼亚胡会同意艾森科特能接受的条件。

sentences.en: And nobody trusts Netanyahu to live up to the promises that that would entail.
sentences.zh: 而且没人相信内塔尼亚胡会信守承诺。

sentences.en: He had a unity government once before.
sentences.zh: 他以前有过一次联合政府。

sentences.en: He promised to step aside and let his partner take over.
sentences.zh: 他承诺会退位让贤，让他的伙伴接手。

sentences.en: You know, he broke the government apart before that happened.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在那发生之前他就拆散了政府。

sentences.en: And, you know, nobody believes that he would live up to it again.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，没人相信他会再次信守承诺。

sentences.en: Also, though, I just sort of wonder what incentive Netanyahu actually has to pretend or try to form a government.
sentences.zh: 不过，我只是有点好奇，内塔尼亚胡到底有什么动力去假装或尝试组建政府。

sentences.en: Because if Eisenkot can't form a government, if Netanyahu can't form a government, if the parliament can't form a government, then everything gets dissolved, right?
sentences.zh: 因为如果艾森科特组阁失败，如果内塔尼亚胡组阁失败，如果议会组阁失败，那么一切都会解散，对吧？

sentences.en: And then there's a new election, which, as you explained, probably breaks Netanyahu's favor.
sentences.zh: 然后就会有新的选举，正如你所解释的，这可能对内塔尼亚胡有利。

sentences.en: So it really just feels like the logical thing, the thing that's in his actual interest, would be to sit back and just let everything fail.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的感觉合乎逻辑的做法，即真正符合他利益的做法，就是坐视一切失败。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, I mean, like, the clock is Netanyahu's friend here, right?
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，时间对内塔尼亚胡来说是朋友，对吧？

sentences.en: So if anybody takes the bait and really takes him seriously, even to get into negotiations in earnest with Netanyahu, is to burn time, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人上钩并真的认真对待他，哪怕是开始与内塔尼亚胡进行认真的谈判，都是在浪费时间，对吧？

sentences.en: Okay, so I understand why partnering with Netanyahu is unlikely and potentially untenable.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我明白为什么与内塔尼亚胡合作是不太可能且可能站不住脚的了。

sentences.en: What about the other options that Eisenkot has?
sentences.zh: 艾森科特还有什么其他选择？

sentences.en: So one option, which he appears to be pursuing right now, is to work with the ultra-Orthodox parties.
sentences.zh: 所以一个他目前似乎正在追求的选择是与极端正统派政党合作。

sentences.en: There's two of them.
sentences.zh: 他们有两个党派。

sentences.en: You know, this is fraught with peril, too.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这也充满了危险。

sentences.en: After all, the ultra-Orthodox have some asks that Eisenkot has vowed to reject.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，极端正统派有一些艾森科特发誓要拒绝的要求。

sentences.en: Above all,
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，

sentences.en: they want to keep their young men from having to serve in the military and protect them against being arrested for draft evasion so that they can continue to study in yeshivas,
sentences.zh: 他们希望让他们的年轻人免于服兵役，并保护他们免受逃避兵役的逮捕，这样他们就可以在成年后继续在经学院学习，

sentences.en: religious schools, throughout their adult lives.
sentences.zh: 也就是宗教学校。

sentences.en: They also want to preserve the very generous government subsidies that allow them to have a lot of babies and raise them and live their lives basically with government funding,
sentences.zh: 他们还希望保留非常慷慨的政府补贴，这让他们能够生很多孩子，抚养他们，基本上靠政府资助生活，

sentences.en: often not really working, you know, private sector jobs or any kind of jobs other than studying in these schools.
sentences.zh: 通常并不真正从事私营部门的工作，或者除了在这些学校学习之外的任何工作。

sentences.en: And Eisenkot and his allies have promised to correct this because, you know, after all,
sentences.zh: 而艾森科特和他的盟友承诺要纠正这一点，因为，你知道，毕竟，

sentences.en: they have run on representing soldiers and reservists who serve in the military and pay the taxes and hold down jobs and whose money they feel is being, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们竞选的口号是代表那些在军队服役、纳税、有正经工作，且他们认为自己的钱被转移给那些不分担负担和牺牲的人的士兵和预备役军人。

sentences.en: shifted to these people who don't share in that burden and sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 所以与极端正统派组建联盟，大概需要艾森科特放弃部分或全部竞选承诺，而这，再次强调，

sentences.en: So to go into a coalition with the ultra-Orthodox would require Eisenkot presumably to have to give up on some or all of those campaign promises, which, again,
sentences.zh: 对于激励选民大量投票至关重要。

sentences.en: was hugely important in inspiring voters to come out in large numbers.
sentences.zh: 不过戴维，还有一件事我觉得非常重要，你在上一集告诉过我们，艾森科特本人是前以色列军队总参谋长。

sentences.en: One other thing, though, David, that I think is really important that you told us in our last episode was that Eisenkot himself is a former Israeli military chief.
sentences.zh: 他在加沙战争中失去了儿子和两个侄子。

sentences.en: He lost a son and two nephews in the war in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 所以他关于每个人都应该服役的纲领，不仅仅是一个纲领。

sentences.en: And so his platform that everybody should serve, it's not just really a platform.
sentences.zh: 这也很大程度上是他个人核心信念的一部分。

sentences.en: It is also very much sort of central to who he is.
sentences.zh: 所以他会突然愿意说，好吧，你知道，我要放弃关于服役和牺牲的核心原则，

sentences.en: And so the idea that he would suddenly be willing to say, OK, you know, I'm going to give up on the central tenant about service and sacrifice,
sentences.zh: 这感觉不像是一个我们所了解的他会急于去做的事情。

sentences.en: it doesn't feel like he would be very eager just as a person what we know about him to do that either.
sentences.zh: 不，确实不是。

sentences.en: No, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，但你触及了一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, but you're getting at something that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 首先，是的，他做出了牺牲。

sentences.en: First, yes, he sacrificed.
sentences.zh: 他相信所有以色列人都应该分担这种牺牲。

sentences.en: He believes that all Israelis should share in the sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这对他来说非常私人。

sentences.en: And it's very personal to him, as you said.
sentences.zh: 然而，在所有反对党中，艾森科特的竞选活动为与极端正统派达成某种协议留下了更多的回旋余地，

sentences.en: However, of all the opposition parties, Eisenkot's campaign left more wiggle room open to doing some kind of a deal with the ultra-Orthodox,
sentences.zh: 当你仔细想想，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: which is very interesting when you think about it.
sentences.zh: 他留下了空间，比如让少数极端正统派免于征兵，虽然比现在的豁免人数少得多，但仍然有一些。

sentences.en: He left room for, like, having a small number of ultra-Orthodox who were exempt from the draft, much smaller than the exemption is now, but still some.
sentences.zh: 他留下了空间来逐步推行一项改革，要求极端正统派学校教授数学、英语和科学等核心课程。

sentences.en: He left room to phase in a shift of, you know, that would require the ultra-Orthodox schools to teach core curriculum subjects like math and English and science.
sentences.zh: 而他们目前并没有这样做。

sentences.en: Which they are not currently doing.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 这样这些人长大后，如果想离开经学院，就能成为社会的生产力成员。

sentences.en: So that these people, when they grow up, can be productive members of society if they want to get out of the yeshivas.
sentences.zh: 但他，你知道，他在这样做的时候稍微宽容了一些，没有那么突兀。

sentences.en: But he, you know, he was a little bit more lenient about doing that not so abruptly.
sentences.zh: 还有其他方式，他似乎在向他们伸出橄榄枝。

sentences.en: There were other ways in which he kind of seemed to be extending, you know, a slight olive branch to them.
